status.label: Reproduce Store/Intune metadata rejection
status.detail: Intune rejects product XP89DCGQ3K6VLD before an installer transaction is identified. Investigate catalog publishing/integration before proposing a PowerToys code change.

next_action.label: Compare Intune catalog metadata
next_action.reason: The report already gives the product ID, exact Intune flow, screenshots and last working release.

reproduce.title: Validate PowerToys Store catalog ingestion by Intune
reproduce.version_requirement: Current Store listing; reported regression from successful 0.81.1 deployment to 0.82.0
prerequisites: An authorized Intune test tenant with permission to add Microsoft Store app (new) applications.
A test Windows device only if the catalog-add stage succeeds; no production assignments or deployment changes.
steps: In the test tenant, add a Windows application using Microsoft Store app (new) and select product XP89DCGQ3K6VLD.

Record whether the catalog-add stage returns 'The selected app does not have a valid latest package version.' Compare the current Store/WinGet catalog version, architecture, scope and installer metadata with the last working 0.81.1 release metadata.
If the app can be added, assign only the test device and compare Company Portal installation to direct supported installation, separating catalog ingestion from installer execution.

Route a catalog-only mismatch to the release/Store publishing and Intune integration owners with the exact field/version comparison. Investigate PowerToys installer code only if an installer actually runs and fails.
reproduce.expected_result: The Store app can be added and installed on a supported test device. If rejected before execution, the evidence identifies a publishing/catalog boundary rather than inventing a PowerToys runtime defect.

judgment.rationale: The exact product ID and Intune add-app flow are already specified. A maintainer with a test tenant can investigate metadata ingestion without another generic reporter request.
evidence: The report names XP89DCGQ3K6VLD and Microsoft Store app (new), with screenshots and the exact validation error.
The reporter identifies 0.81.1 as the last successful Company Portal deployment.
Live issue has no comments or assignees; no timeline-linked or direct issue-number fixing PR was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce in an Intune test tenant and compare release catalog metadata before selecting an owner or code patch.

fix_assessment.rationale: No PowerToys source-code fix is currently substantiated: the reported add-app rejection is at the external Store/Intune catalog boundary before a PowerToys installer transaction is shown. A release metadata or integration correction may be needed; this classification does not assert that Intune is at fault, that the report is by design, or that the open bug should be closed.

issue_context.summary: Intune refuses the PowerToys Store product as a new managed app and existing Company Portal deployments also stop installing after a previously working 0.81.1 release.
known_information: PowerToys version 0.82.0 is reported and product ID XP89DCGQ3K6VLD is explicit.
The report supplies two screenshots, the precise add-app method and 'no valid latest package version' error.
The live open issue has Issue-Bug, Area-Setup/Install and Area-Enterprise labels, no comments and no assignee.
inferences: The add-app error suggests catalog ingestion/installer metadata validation, not a proven runtime or MSI failure.
The simultaneous failure of existing deployment entries may involve the same published metadata, but this has not been verified.
issue_context.analysis: A useful next step is maintainer-side comparison of Store metadata and tenant behavior. Do not ask the reporter to supply normal PowerToys logs for a flow that may never launch PowerToys, and do not claim external fault without reproducing.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and confirmed there are no comments or assigned owners.
Checked the public timeline and a direct issue-number PR search; no concrete fix attempt was identified.
Located the failure boundary from the report's catalog-add step and established deployment method. No Intune tenant or live Store metadata comparison was performed.

information_gaps.information: Current catalog ingestion result and the metadata field or integration step responsible for rejection.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines whether release publishing, Intune integration or an executed installer needs correction.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer follows the authorized test-tenant reproduction, recording only public package metadata and sanitized error details.
